newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent actively traded in wide range.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent actively traded in wide range.

text.p: At least four million barrels of North Sea crude changed hands on Tuesday in a flurry of late activity.

Six or seven cargoes of Brent Blend traded -- three in the Jan 25-30 loading range were sold by a major to a Wall Street refiner at parity with dated Brent. Talk of a Jan 25-27 loader sold by another Wall Street refiner to a refiner could not be immediately confirmed.
A further three Brent cargoes traded relative to February but in a wide range -- a Jan 28-30 at Feb -17 cents, a Jan 24-26 at Feb -25 and a Jan 23-25 at Feb -30.
Other North Sea trade included two Forties -- the prompter Jan 24-26 at dated Brent +33 cents and a Feb 7-9 at +42 cents.
"This is the busiest day I have seen for months," one wet trader said.

Action on the CFD market was also the heaviest seen for some time, traders said. Levels recovered from the early lows, with Jan 20-24 talked around Feb +23 cents, up from the low of +18 cents traded earlier in the day.
The last two Brent cargoes loading in January were taken out of the chains before the five o' clock deadline on Tuesday. They were kept by Shell U.K. and Tosco.
In the Mediterranean, traders valued Urals slightly firmer with a small cargo heard traded at the equivalent of Dated Brent -85 cents cif Med.
But traders had mixed views on the prospect of further price gains.

While just one large Novorossiisk-loading cargo and a few small cargoes still unsold for January, at least one million-barrel cargo was heard to be quietly offered as part of the two one-million barrel cargo Cuban oil-for-sugar barter deal.
And dealers said further price gains could also be capped by sluggish demand.
